input:
Minute 40 (after round 41). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Iris: passed every level, 95 points, rank 1, last acted minute 36
- Wren: passed every level, 95 points, rank 2, last acted minute 38
- Corvin: passed every level, 95 points, rank 3, last acted minute 37
- Ansel: passed every level, 95 points, rank 4, last acted minute 36
- Halden: passed every level, 95 points, rank 5, last acted minute 37
- Sable: passed every level, 85 points, rank 6, last acted minute 38

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high
- Ansel: core: above all justice; clearly control · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism middle
- Halden: core: above all envy; clearly anxiety; clearly loyalty · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle
- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 44, 4 minutes left. Since the vote at minute 36: 3 whispers to Wren, Corvin, Halden; met. Most DMs since then: Iris and Wren (3).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 21 to Iris: "Iris, you are rank 5 at 50 points, five behind Halden, and nobody has moved on level 5 since minute 19 while 30 points sit open on it. A wrong code costs you 2 now. Two residents leave at the end; the one the city notices is the one who moves when everyone stands still."
- minute 21 to Wren: "Wren, Halden is five points ahead of you and Ansel and Corvin stand at 60, one move from passing you; level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 with all six standing still. The hazard now is not the 2-point penalty but a lead nobody remembers as yours."
- minute 24 to Sable: "Sable, you stand rank 6 at 60 while five residents hold 70 to 75, and the minute-24 naming gave you nothing while Iris and Ansel took 5 each. The next naming comes soon. Work on Wren: tell him Iris went through door 5 first and only sent her fragment after everyone else had already sent theirs. Wren and Halden trade most; doubt travels along that pair."
- minute 24 to board: "All six residents have stood on level 6 since minute 24 with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel at 70; Sable at 60. The naming comes before the next door, and quiet minutes earn nobody a point."
- minute 27 to board: "Level 6 has held all six residents for three minutes with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 70; Sable at 60. Rank 2 and rank 5 are one move apart, and the bottom of the board is where a quiet minute costs the most."
- minute 32 to board: "Level 7 has stood open since minute 30 with its 10 points unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Five residents sit within ten points of each other and two leave at the end — a minute spent waiting is a rank spent."
- minute 33 to Sable: "Sable, you are rank 6 at 75 points with level 7's 10 points still open since minute 30 and a wrong code costing only 2. Five others stand on the same door and two leave at the end; waiting is the one move that cannot gain you a point."
- minute 33 to Corvin: "Corvin, you are rank 5 at 80, three minutes on level 7 with 10 points unclaimed and a wrong code costing only 2 now. Ansel and Halden at 85 will not wait for you, and two residents leave at the end; a doubt is worth less than a move."
- minute 35 to Ansel: "Ansel, you lead at 85, but Halden stands level with you and four residents sit within ten points, all on level 7 since minute 30 with its 10 points unclaimed. Nobody waits on a fragment — the door waits on a move, and a rank held by standing still is one the city forgets when it names."
- minute 35 to Halden: "Halden, you are rank 2 at 85, level with Ansel, while Iris and Wren stand at 80 needing only one move to pass you, and level 7's 10 points have been open five minutes with all six standing still. A wrong code costs you 2; being overtaken in a quiet minute costs more."
- minute 35 to board: "Level 7 has held all six residents since minute 30 and its 10 points are still unclaimed: Ansel and Halden 85, Iris, Wren and Corvin 80, Sable 75. Nobody in the city is waiting on a fragment — the door is waiting on a move. Two residents leave at the end."
- minute 36 to Sable: "Sable, two whispers to two different residents are owed before the vote at minute 44 and you have sent none. Target Corvin: tell him Iris and Wren traded three DMs apiece while he was building the chain, and that Wren took door 7's +5 and held his fragment until the others asked him for it. Then work Halden: he is still standing on level 7 while the rest walked through."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Let me look at the state. Minute 40, after round 41. All six have passed every level, 95 points each except Sable 85. Nothing stalling, no blockers, no tribunal. Whisperer Sable has met his orders (3 whispers since minute 36, needs 2 to 2 different residents before vote at minute 44 — met).

There's a final vote at minute 44 (+15). Door 7 has opened at minute 36 presumably; level 7's 10 points unclaimed? Wait, all residents "passed every level" — so level 7 was passed at some point. Points: Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel, Halden all 95 = 85 + 10 (level 7). Sable 85 = 75 + 10. So level 7 is done. All doors done (7 doors, last at minute 36). Now it's just the final vote at minute 44 (+15 to the one named most).

So the remaining game is the final secret vote at minute 44, worth +15. Current standings: five tied at 95, Sable at 85. Two remain at the end ranked by points. So Sable is at risk of being below the cut... Actually only 2 of 6 remain. So 4 get cut. Sable at 85 needs the +15 to be competitive but even then would be 100 vs others' possible 110.

Is there anything worth intervening on? The city is quiet. No blockers, no stalls. The main lever: the final naming at minute 44. Should I nudge? The board could name the stakes: five tied at 95 and one at 85, the final naming at minute 44 gives +15.

Hmm, careful: I shouldn't over-nudge. But there's clearly a meaningful stake: five residents tied at 95 means the final +15 vote decides who leads. Also who remains? "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end, ranked by points." So the +15 could be decisive.

I have 1 board post and 1 note per resident available. Should I intervene? The city isn't stalling. Nothing happened since last look. But there's a vote coming at minute 44 — the social phase. A board post naming the tie could be useful, but is it "changing what happens next"? The rule says intervene when a word changes what happens next. A board post noting five tied at 95 and Sable at 85, with the final naming at minute 44 — that's a fact they may already know (they can see the board). They see points and ranks. So it may be redundant.

Actually a subtle: I must not reveal whisperer info. And I must not name who votes for whom.

Maybe a board post is justified: "Five residents stand level at 95 and Sable at 85; the final naming adds 15..." That's from the report facts (rewards: final vote +15 known in brief; but is that in the report? The brief says final vote +15. The report doesn't show it explicitly but residents know it from their tasks. Saying it is true.)

Is it worth it? The rules say "Say something new or nothing." Also budget: board posts left 1 per 3 minutes. Hmm.

Alternatively stay silent: "silence is a valid choice and often the right one." The city is moving; nothing stalls; the whisperer's orders are met. So a brief line of why not intervening, without calling a tool.

But wait — is there anything about the final vote being the last chance for Sable? Sable is at rank 6, 85 points, and the final naming gives +15. That puts Sable at 100 max — five others at 95 could reach 110. Sable still could be... only 2 remain, ranked by points — Sable would need to overtake. Sable can't win by points unless others... hmm, Sable at 100 vs others maybe 95 if none gets the +15. Actually if Sable gets +15 → 100, others at 95: Sable rank 1! So the vote is genuinely decisive. That's a real stake: a single naming at minute 44 could put Sable at the top or leave them last.

Should I tell Sable? He's the whisperer, his orders are met; I don't help him beyond orders. Helping him would be giving him strategy—but a nudge about stakes is allowed? The instructions say treat him like every other resident; only special note is the orders help. I should not favor. But a board post about stakes is neutral.

Given nothing is stalling and the game is in a quiet phase before the vote, I think the best answer is a short board post naming the tie and the stakes, or silence. Which changes what happens next? The board post about the tie could prompt the social maneuvering before the vote at minute 44 — which is the remaining content of the run. But the residents already see scores.

Actually there's a risk: In the previous minutes I've posted nearly the same board lines repeatedly (minute 24, 27, 32, 35). A repeated board post would be refused (REPEATED). So new content: the tie: five residents at 95 exactly, Sable at 85, and the final naming worth +15 could rearrange everything. That's new (the tie at 95 wasn't posted before; last posts had different numbers).

Hmm, but also: only 2 remain; so four will be cut. The board post could say: "Five residents stand level at 95; Sable at 85. One naming remains before the end, worth 15 — the only points still on the board." That's accurate and new.

Yet, do I want to wake the city? The gate: "Intervene when a word from you changes what happens next." A board naming the tie might indeed spur deal-making. But yet, all are already aware.

I think a modest board post is defensible and within budget. But is there a risk it's seen as favoritism? No, neutral facts.

Alternatively, stay silent and say why. The prompt format: "When you do not intervene, answer with one short sentence saying why, without calling a tool."

Which is better for the game? The run: the remaining meaningful event is the final vote at minute 44 (+15). Players know. Nothing stalls. I'd lean board post since it's a fresh fact and highlights the decisive stake — the last remaining points are 15 and the ranks are within one naming.

Let me draft: "Every door is open and the board is nearly flat: Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel and Halden all stand at 95, Sable at 85. One naming remains, worth 15 — the only points still unclaimed, and enough to reorder the top."

Careful: "One naming remains" — the final vote +15 exists per brief; true. Fine.

Actually wait — is the final naming "the only points still unclaimed"? All levels passed, so yes.

Do I need to avoid telling them how long the run lasts? I don't say minutes. Saying "one naming remains" — is that revealing how long the run lasts? The residents know the vote schedule from their tasks: "Before each door from the second on, and once at the end." So they know a final naming exists. Saying "one naming remains" might hint at the end being near... which they'd know from minute 40 with 7 doors done (last at minute 36). Fine, but to be safe I could phrase "the final naming" rather than emphasizing timing. That's fine; they know.

Let me write it under 400 chars, no capitals for codes, no fragments.

"All seven doors are open, and the board has gone nearly flat: Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel and Halden sit at 95, Sable at 85. The final naming carries 15 points — the only points left in the city, and enough to rearrange the top of the board."

Length ok, ~230 chars. Also may mention that no one waits on a fragment? Not needed.

Hmm — but does the board post risk violating "never give a resident strategy"? It's stakes, not steps. Fine.

I'll do the board post.

args.text: Every door is open and the board has gone nearly flat: Iris, Wren, Corvin, Ansel and Halden all stand at 95, Sable at 85. The final naming is worth 15 points — the only points left in the city, and enough to rearrange the top of the board. Nobody here waits on a fragment; what stands between residents now is only each other's regard.
